topic: binance hackers use fake job interviews for $6.3b heist
headline_marked: Binance: [[North Korean hackers]] used fake job interviews & AI tool for $6.3B heist
headline: Binance: North Korean hackers used fake job interviews & AI tool for $6.3B heist
summary: Hackers reportedly used a malicious Google ad, a tampered installer, and a fake interview assignment to gain backdoor access, leading to the largest crypto theft to date.
details: Binance has detailed how North Korean hackers, identified as 'TraderTraitor' by the FBI, executed the record-breaking $6.3 billion crypto heist. The attack began in June with a malicious Google ad leading to a tampered installer, which compromised one developer's machine.

A second, more sophisticated attack occurred in September when an engineer was targeted with a fake job interview. This involved multiple rounds of interviews and social media engagement to build trust, culminating in the engineer downloading malware disguised as an interview assignment.

This malware replaced a legitimate development tool component with a malicious version, granting attackers backdoor access. Binance stated that its security tools failed to detect this 0-day malware due to its advanced obfuscation and evasion techniques.

By October, the hackers leveraged Binance's own internal AI tool to gain control over wallets belonging to the two compromised employees. This allowed them to initiate unauthorized transfers, leading to the massive theft.

Binance explained that the use of Multi-Party Computation (MPC) for its hot wallet prevented an immediate revocation of authorizations, complicating efforts to stop the transactions. However, the company has since replenished 98% of the impacted tokens and resumed withdrawals.

While Binance has prevented numerous North Korean-linked cyber threats, the specifics of how this particular attack succeeded, especially the role of the internal AI tool and the failure of security measures against the malware, remain points of concern and investigation.

topic: apple watch introduces audio intelligence and third-party app access for siri
headline_marked: Apple [[gives Siri AI access]] to third-party apps with iOS 27.3
headline: Apple gives Siri AI access to third-party apps with iOS 27.3
summary: Siri AI can now perform actions across your favorite apps, leveraging on-screen awareness and natural language processing to complete requests.
details: Apple is significantly expanding Siri AI's capabilities with the rollout of iOS 27.3, allowing the voice assistant to interact with third-party applications.

Developers can now integrate Siri AI features into their apps, enabling it to understand user context, process natural language prompts, and use on-screen awareness to complete requests without explicit app name mentions.

A new 'app skills' feature allows developers to combine multiple tasks into a single Siri command, streamlining complex actions. For example, users can change a ride-sharing pickup location by simply asking Siri.

Siri AI's enhanced abilities will also be integrated into Apple's own apps, including Calendar, Files, Mail, Maps, Messages, Notes, and Safari, allowing for more intuitive data retrieval and management.
This update aims to make Siri AI a more powerful and versatile assistant, capable of handling a wider range of tasks and providing a more seamless user experience across the Apple ecosystem.
